solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Palms demitasse's held in

indicators.note: something held in another word sits inside it, so the letters are found running within the next word

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word for a small coffee cup

explanation.surface: A tiny coffee cup cradled in someone's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palms' looks like hands round the cup, but it is the definition. The 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ita is a South American palm tree, so the plural names several of those trees.

clue.text: In the view of doctor, hospital ward closure limits resistance for mite with parasitic larva

indicators.note: to limit something is to set bounds round it, so the other letters close round the one for resistance

parts.note: as in 'to me' meaning 'in my view'
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A doctor's opinion that shutting a hospital ward restricts resistance to mites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the view of' gives TO as in 'to my mind'; MB is the British medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombiculids are harvest mites, whose larvae, called chiggers, feed on animals and people as parasites.

clue.text: Odds on bot developed around algorithmic software as lure for trolling?

parts.note: starting price, the betting odds at the off

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on either side of the software abbreviation
something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An internet troll bot built on AI, with the odds on it working.
explanation.walkthrough: Trolling here is not online abuse but a fishing method: dragging a lure behind a moving boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoonbait is a spoon-shaped metal lure that wobbles when pulled through water, used when fishing by trolling.

clue.text: Disgusted comments about shortage of tennis equipment and ancient cover for horse

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for disgusted comments is read from the end
a shortage means something is missing, here the final letter of the equipment

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about missing tennis kit and an antique horse blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A shabracque is a cavalry saddle-cloth, an old ornamental covering laid over a horse's back under the saddle.

clue.text: Die, picking up carbon in black slime

indicators.note: in a down entry picking something up lifts it, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

indicators.note: in puts the carbon symbol inside the word for slime

explanation.surface: Something dies after taking in carbon while sitting in black ooze.
explanation.walkthrough: The C goes into MUCUS after B, and the whole string is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give way, and in particular to give way to illness or injury and pass away.

clue.text: Welsh son of rugby player favoured formula that bars English getting close

indicators.note: to bar something is to keep it out, so the letter for English is excluded from the formula

parts.note: a forward in the front row of the scrum

explanation.surface: A Welsh rugby player's son backs a winning formula that shuts out the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropinquation is a formal Latinate word for drawing near or approaching something.

clue.text: It's true about court seizing current account

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for true wraps round what follows
seizing means grabbing hold, so the court abbreviation holds the current symbol

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A sworn statement about a court case catching up with a current account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current account' looks like banking, but current is electrical and account is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed narration or telling of facts, so it is an account of events.

clue.text: Maiden engaged by Elizabeth possibly shortened her devoted poet's suit

indicators.note: something engaged by another is taken on inside it, so the maiden's letter goes within
shortened means cut down, so the last letter of the royal title goes

parts.note: Elizabeth I or II as an example of a queen
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A maiden in Queen Elizabeth's service and the poet who adored her.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet devoted to Elizabeth I is Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene; the definition asks for his word.
explanation.definitionFit: Queme is a Spenserian verb meaning to please or be fitting, so in his usage it means to suit.

clue.text: Minute enemy's wasted with minutes to spare

indicators.note: wasted suggests something ruined or broken up, so the remaining letters are scrambled
something to spare is left over and can go, so the minutes letter is taken out

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.surface: The enemy has been destroyed with minutes left on the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like a unit of time to match 'minutes', but it is the adjective pronounced my-NEWT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eensy is a childish word meaning very tiny, as in eensy-weensy, matching minute in the sense of small.

clue.text: Policeman protecting island or returning keeps himself involved with fingerprints

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so the policeman wraps round the next two words
returning means going back the way it came, so the whole guarded string is read from right to left
to keep something is to hold it inside, so the turned string takes the policeman in again

parts.note: the same policeman again, referred to by the pronoun

explanation.surface: A police officer guarding an island returns and stays busy with fingerprint evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Himself' points back to the policeman, so the same word is used twice: first as the outer guard, then once more tucked inside after the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Poroscopy identifies people from the sweat pores in fingerprint ridges, so poroscopic describes work involving fingerprints.

clue.text: With this and many more you'll have won judge a lot of time

definitions.text: With this and many more you'll have won

parts.note: an age, a vast span of time

explanation.surface: A judge promises that a long stretch of effort will bring victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Won' looks like the past tense of win, but it is the currency of South Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: The jeon is the Korean coin worth a hundredth of a won, so a hundred of them make one.

clue.text: Humanity in Cape Horn wearing uniform repeatedly

indicators.note: a thing wearing clothes is covered by them, so the uniform letters go on either side

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet, taken twice
to bunt is to butt with the horns

explanation.surface: A sailor in uniform rounding Cape Horn again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape Horn' reads as one place, but Cape belongs to the definition (the Western Cape of South Africa) and Horn is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubuntu is a Southern African philosophy of shared humanity and kindness toward others, prominent in the Cape region.

clue.text: Properly speaking, expansion of N1 without any new empty property

indicators.note: without any means every one of them is removed, not just a single instance

parts.note: N1 written out in full as North One, a London postcode

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides cleared out, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Developing a London postcode district with no new building on empty property.
explanation.walkthrough: N1 is the postcode for Islington in north London; spelled out it has three Ns, and all of them go.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthoepy is the study or practice of correct pronunciation, so it means speaking properly as a discipline.

clue.text: Vineyard pests from pub mounted raid across high fence

parts.note: public house, as on a map

indicators.note: lying across something means stretched over it, so the turned raid word spans the fence
in a down clue something mounted climbs upward, so the raid word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a tall jumping fence in equestrian events

explanation.surface: Pests coming out of the pub to raid a vineyard over its fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Phylloxeras are tiny aphid-like insects that attack grapevine roots and devastated European vineyards in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Minutes from part of play area

parts.note: a play is divided into acts

explanation.surface: Timing a section of a drama or a playground.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta are official records of proceedings, the formal minutes of a meeting or court.

clue.text: Brown horses crossing sort of wilder places to lead them

indicators.note: the horses straddle the rearranged letters, sitting on both sides of them

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

indicators.note: a sort of something is a version of it, so these letters come out in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Brown horses roam across rougher country, to places where riders take them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points back to the horses of the surface, so the definition only makes sense in context.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridleways are public tracks for riders, where people lead or ride horses but cars are not allowed.

clue.text: Judicious US research university will put up with dope going round

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the drug word surrounds the raised letters
in a down clue putting something up raises it, so these letters are read upwards

explanation.surface: An American university tolerating drug use on campus, a wise move.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-timed is done at an opportune moment, which shows good judgment, as a judicious act does.

clue.text: Vigorously descriptive line early in The Flask etc, which Baudelaire wrote

indicators.note: early in says the line letter is given an earlier place within the next word than it normally has

parts.note: French for 'which', as a French poet would write it

explanation.surface: A line from a French poem about a flask, quoted by Baudelaire.
explanation.walkthrough: The line letter is promoted from fifth place to second within the flasks word; Baudelaire was a French poet, hence the French word for which.
explanation.definitionFit: Blottesque describes painting or writing done in bold heavy strokes, and so means vigorously and broadly depicted.

clue.text: Welsh chief giving away gallons (litres) is a generous person?

indicators.note: giving something away means parting with it, so the gallons and litres letters are lost

parts.note: Owen Glendower, the medieval Welsh leader who rebelled against English rule

explanation.surface: A Welsh chieftain handing out drink by the gallon is a generous host.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets show the litres go along with the gallons; both letters leave GLENDOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: An endower gives an endowment, a gift of money or property, so the question mark flags a generous donor.

clue.text: Space on medal, back of George Cross, before being filled with endless resin

indicators.note: filled with means something is placed inside, so the shortened resin goes into the word for before
the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the name is kept

parts.note: a cross is shaped like X

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the resin word is dropped

explanation.surface: The reverse of a George Cross medal is coated in resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George Cross' reads as the British gallantry award, but the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: An exergue is the small space on a coin or medal below the main design, often holding a date or inscription.

clue.text: Maybe one of bagpiper's fingerholes, all left short of second base part

indicators.note: a letter short of a stroke has lost part of its shape, turning it into a different letter

parts.note: L for left in every one of the four places
the horizontal foot of the second letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: A piper's fingerholes all lie to the left of the second part of the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A visual trick: an L without its foot stroke is an upright line, which reads as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lill is an old Scots word for a hole in the chanter of a bagpipe, which the piper covers with a finger.

clue.text: Pilgrim festival's primitive instincts united youth with bit of a laugh

parts.note: the id is the instinctive part of the psyche in Freud's model
a single ha is part of a laugh

explanation.surface: A festival brings out basic instincts and youthful fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Id-ul-Adha is the Muslim Feast of Sacrifice, held at the end of the annual Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca.

clue.text: God fundamentally involved in distribution of rain?

definitions.text: God fundamentally involved in distribution of rain?

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it
distribution spreads things around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: at the base or bottom of the word, so only its final letter in a down entry

explanation.surface: Asking whether a deity is behind where rain falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indra is the Hindu god of the heavens, thunder and rain, so he is the deity who sends it.

clue.text: Spades knocked off certainly are known to rust

indicators.note: knocked off means removed, so the letter for spades is struck out

parts.note: 'sure do' is a casual affirmative, reading 'certainly' plus 'are known to' as in 'they do'

explanation.surface: Garden spades, left out, are bound to go rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are known to' looks like a link before the definition, but it supplies DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is an old name for a rust fungus, or the rust-coloured spore stage of such fungi on plants.

clue.text: Second person to take a cab ride reported good arrangement

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we want the sound rather than the spelling

parts.words: Second person to take a cab ride
parts.note: you is the second person pronoun; to taxi is to ride in a cab

explanation.surface: Someone tells a second party to grab a taxi, a neat plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Eutaxy is an orderly or well-ordered disposition of parts, from Greek for good order.

clue.text: Jackal halved progressive plant deteriorations

indicators.note: halved means cut in two, so only the first half of the eight letters stays

parts.note: dieback is a plant disease that kills shoots from the tips inward

explanation.surface: A jackal gets half the blame for a garden blight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieb is a North African jackal, a wild dog of the deserts.

clue.text: Scottish rebel beginning to win hearts, bigger in Italy with initial majority overturned

indicators.note: only the opening stretch that makes up more than half the word is flipped round, the rest staying put
the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: Italian for bigger, as in Lago Maggiore

explanation.surface: A rebel's opening gambit is to win hearts, with most of Italy's backing turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial majority' means the first five of the word's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiggamores were 17th-century Scottish Covenanters who marched on Edinburgh in 1648, the origin of the party name Whig.

clue.text: Liberal banned from full-on organised church until death

indicators.note: banned from means excluded, so the liberal letter is thrown out of the word for full-on

explanation.surface: A Liberal is barred from an all-out church organisation for life.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Ls goes.
explanation.definitionFit: À l'outrance is French for to the utmost, describing a fight continued to the bitter end, until one side dies.

clue.text: Not a word on Delaware Indian's homeland

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another is placed after it, so the silence call follows the state

parts.note: postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about a Delaware Native American's ancestral land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delaware Indian' reads as a Lenape person; the Indian is actually from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Desh is the Hindi and Bengali word for country or native land, as in Bangladesh.
